speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your response. To better understand your condition, can you describe any recent history of fever, weight loss, or difficulty swallowing? Also, have you noticed any changes in your speech or facial movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty closing your eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning because your symptoms of fluctuating weakness and specific diplopia do not align with Tuberculosis. I need to rule out other causes; can you tell me if your eyelids droop significantly or if your speech becomes slurred when you speak for a long time? Also, when was your last dose of medication for TB?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal results for creatine kinase, TSH, and neck ultrasound help rule out myasthenia gravis, thyroid eye disease, and structural causes like tumors. Since your symptoms fluctuate with activity and specific maneuvers, I need to confirm if your ptosis and diplopia worsen immediately after sustained upward gaze or looking down at your feet. Have you noticed any recent infections or fatigue that precede the worsening of your muscle weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis (MS)

The absence of swallowing difficulties, the specific nature of your diplopia worsening with gaze direction, and the gradual onset over a month point more strongly towards a demyelinating condition like MS rather than a neuromuscular junction disorder. Can you tell me if you have experienced any numbness, tingling, or electric shock sensations in your limbs or trunk?
